title: Understanding Vectors in C++
summary: Learn what a vector is and how to use it in C++.

scenes.narration: Welcome to our lesson on vectors in C++.
scenes.heading: Understanding Vectors in C++
scenes.subheading: Learn what a vector is and how to use it in C++

scenes.narration: First, we include the iostream and vector libraries.
We start our main function here.
Here, we declare a vector named numbers that will hold integers.
We add the numbers 10, 20, and 30 to our vector using push back.
Now, our vector contains just one element, 10.
After adding 20, our vector now has two elements.
Finally, after adding 30, our vector contains three elements.
We use a range-based for loop to iterate through each element in the vector and print it.
This is the output of our program, displaying all the elements in the vector.
In this lesson, we learned about vectors in C++, how to add elements to them, and how to display those elements.
points: Vectors are dynamic arrays that can grow and shrink in size.
We use push back to add elements to a vector.
Range-based for loops are useful for iterating over elements in a vector.
